summary_oneline: Re-base the accounting metrics layer as a parrot.semantic.accounting sub-package of the shipped ai-parrot-semantic, keeping its accounting compiler and adding the in-process DuckDB-over-Arrow runtime that nothing provides today

constraints.statement: The satellite, its workspace source, release entry, CI step, nightly matrix entry and the duckdb extra already exist and are pinned by tests/test_packaging.py with equality assertions
constraints.implication: the revision creates no packaging; any new dependency or extra must update test_packaging.py in the same task

constraints.statement: parrot/semantic/__init__.py eagerly imports SemanticLayerToolkit while the README requires the accounting extension to remain independently importable
constraints.implication: 'independently importable' is not true today; the revision must either make the package __init__ lazy and test the independence, or drop the requirement

constraints.statement: engines.compile instantiates NativeCompiler directly and the semantic-layer spec records 'single compiler with no dispatch'; the native grammar is measures/dimensions/joins
constraints.implication: the accounting compiler is a second, parallel compiler inside the package, not an engine plug-in; its relation to the reserved FEAT-742 Rust compiler must be stated

constraints.statement: The shipped layer executes through Executor over DatabaseQueryToolkit with env-named connections and dict rows; the old spec executed through SQLToolkit.execute_query
constraints.implication: two database execution stacks exist; the revision must choose one for the 'database' target

constraints.statement: DuckDB is used only as a queried database: one short-lived connection per query in DuckDBSource, read-only for files; nothing registers frames, keeps a root connection or returns Arrow
constraints.implication: the DuckDB-over-Arrow runtime of old M6 is entirely new code and cannot be built on DuckDBSource

constraints.statement: SemanticAuditLedger already provides signing, storage(json_str) and fail-closed-when-required, but it is typed to SemanticAuditEntry, stores SQL text and user_id, retains entries in memory, and requires durability only when a sink is configured
constraints.implication: reusing it needs a generalised entry contract; keeping a separate AccountingAuditLedger duplicates about one module

constraints.statement: The shipped PBAC posture is fail-closed over DataPlanePolicyGuard with table-level resources and per-role member grants from a mandatory policy side-file; the old spec used DatasetPolicyGuard with 'no guard => allow' and accounting:<tenant>:<model>:<metric> resources
constraints.implication: two opposite governance postures would live in one package unless the revision aligns them

constraints.statement: The semantic loader reads one flat models directory with no tenant level; the old spec placed models at <models_dir>/<tenant>/<model>.yaml
constraints.implication: tenant scoping of accounting models is a layout decision the revision must restate against the shipped convention

constraints.statement: DatasetManager keeps datasets as pandas frames on entry._df, read directly from many sites in tool.py, with a Redis Parquet cache; no DuckDB- or Arrow-backed store exists and no recent commit or branch touches storage
constraints.implication: a DuckDB-backed dataset store is a cross-cutting DatasetManager change, distinct from a DuckDB runtime that only reads frames through a frame_provider

constraints.statement: FEAT-880 moved the DuckDB-backed dataset store 'into a revision of FEAT-713', while the old FEAT-713 spec lists 'Modifying DatasetManager' as a non-goal (codex S7)
constraints.implication: the two documents contradict each other; the owner must say which scope the revision takes

constraints.statement: pyarrow>=25.0 is a core dependency; duckdb is declared only as the semantic satellite's extra; polars is declared nowhere
constraints.implication: AC17 already holds; the polars half of AC10 needs an optional import or must be dropped

constraints.statement: Core integration points named by the old spec still resolve; the CLI registry and register_object_schedules anchors moved, docs/semantic/ does not exist (docs live in wiki/tools/semantic-layer.md), and no scheduler construction was found in ai-parrot-server
constraints.implication: M8-M10 anchors must be refreshed; the scheduled validation still has no verified call site

new: parrot.semantic.accounting sub-package inside the existing satellite: contracts and error taxonomy (old M2), closed metric grammar (old M3), chart snapshot + loader + per-interval validation (old M4), deterministic sqlglot compiler with cumulative windows, hashing, lineage, self-check and per-dialect golden tests (old M5)

In-process DuckDB-over-Arrow runtime: one root connection, Arrow-registered frames, per-thread cursors under asyncio.to_thread, duckdb imported lazily through require_extra — the first of its kind in the repository
Database runtime for the same compiled query (executor choice is U1)
AccountingToolkit with tool_prefix 'finance' (list/explain/query/validate), a 'parrot finance' CLI command and an MCP-local config example
Live validation (assertions + chart drift) on demand and scheduled
Accounting audit record carrying model_hash, snapshot_hash, sql_hash, lineage_ref, assertion status and target (ledger reuse is U1)
Documentation as an accounting section under the wiki/tools convention plus a README update

replace 'future accounting extension' with the actual layering contract
only if a dependency or extra is added (e.g. polars)

untouched: Satellite packaging, release entry, CI step and nightly matrix (old M1, AC2, the 'test-semantic' job of AC16) — already delivered by FEAT-704
The generic NativeCompiler, engines.compile, GovernancePipeline and the sl_* tools

Lowering accounting metrics into the generic layer and the FEAT-742 Rust compiler

patterns.pattern: compile off the event loop with asyncio.to_thread plus a compile cache keyed by model digest, canonical request and dialect
sign canonical_bytes() (sorted-key JSON without signature) with AbstractKMSSigner and forward model_dump_json() to an async storage callable
single governed entry path in the toolkit (authorize, rights, compile, execute, audit) and a _pre_execute check for a bound PermissionContext
DuckDB work inside asyncio.to_thread with a lazy import and a clear error when the extra is missing; governed DuckDB files opened read-only
pandas to Arrow through pa.Table.from_pandas, as the REPL worker transport does
lazy CLI command registration with an extras hint

risks.risk: Two compilers and two governance postures in one package
risks.impact: users and FEAT-742 cannot tell which rules apply to a finance metric; mitigate by stating the layering contract and aligning PBAC/audit with the shipped layer (U1, U2)

risks.risk: Scope creep from the DuckDB-backed dataset store
risks.impact: rewriting DatasetManager storage inside an accounting feature multiplies its size and blast radius; mitigate by deciding U3 before the spec
an accounting import pulls parrot.auth, databasequery and jsonschema; mitigate with a subprocess import test
the shipped contracts return dict rows with no Decimal handling, and pandas to Arrow copies and may carry object/float amounts; mitigate with the old AC9 rules and conversion errors
the only existing DuckDB code opens one connection per query; the root-connection/per-thread-cursor design has no in-repo precedent and needs a concurrency test

risks.risk: Scheduled validation has no verified call site
risks.impact: old Q11 is still open; mitigate by resolving it in the spec or shipping on-demand validation first

risks.risk: Golden SQL drift on a sqlglot bump
risks.impact: the pin sqlglot>=30.1,<31 is shared with the generic compiler; a bump now changes both

confidence_map.reasoning: packaging files, tests, merge history and the semantic-layer spec U6 all read directly

confidence_map.statement: The reason FEAT-713 was standalone (FEAT-704 paused on an AGPL dependency) no longer exists; the package ships a clean-room native sqlglot compiler
confidence_map.reasoning: dependency list, packaging test banning the removed module, rev2 decision

confidence_map.statement: The generic compiler cannot express the accounting model (account sets, sign normalisation, effective-dated membership, cumulative windows, reconciliation assertions), so the accounting compiler remains a separate component
confidence_map.reasoning: native.py was read only to line 140 and the wiki outline shows none of these; absence beyond line 140 is inferred

confidence_map.statement: There is no engine seam to plug an accounting compiler into
No in-process DuckDB engine over registered frames and no Arrow result path exists anywhere in package sources
confidence_map.reasoning: grep over package sources for duckdb imports, register and fetch_arrow_table

confidence_map.statement: AC17 already holds: pyarrow is a core dependency and duckdb is only an extra of the satellite
The signed, fail-closed audit mechanics of old M7 already exist in SemanticAuditLedger; only the entry shape and the default mode differ
The old spec's PBAC, executor, tenant layout and audit-mode choices each conflict with what the shipped layer does
confidence_map.reasoning: both sides read: old spec inventory and shipped modules

confidence_map.statement: The accounting-domain design of old M2-M5 (contracts, grammar, loader/validation, compiler, goldens) does not depend on the package state and carries over unchanged
confidence_map.reasoning: inferred: none of those modules cites a FEAT-704 premise, but name collisions (Grain, Metric) and shared sqlglot pin need a pass in the spec

confidence_map.statement: A DuckDB-backed dataset store and the frame_provider-fed DuckDB runtime are different features; the first rewrites DatasetManager storage, the second touches none of it
confidence_map.reasoning: entry._df accessor inventory and old spec non-goal read directly

confidence_map.reasoning: from the FEAT-880 proposal text and its F014; the FEAT-880 spec in progress was not read

confidence_map.statement: Old integration points still resolve, with two moved anchors, no docs/semantic/ directory and no verified scheduler call site in the server
confidence_map.reasoning: each symbol grepped; the scheduler absence is a negative grep result

confidence_map.statement: Collision risk is low: no unmerged branch touches the semantic package, an accounting area or dataset storage, and FEAT-742 has no branch

confidence_map.statement: The revised feature is roughly the old M2-M10 minus M1, with M6-M8 re-based; it remains a multi-task feature of similar size

unknowns.question: May parrot.semantic.accounting reuse the shipped semantic infrastructure (audit ledger, Executor/ConnectionResolver over DatabaseQueryToolkit, compile cache), or does it stay standalone as originally designed (own AccountingAuditLedger, DatabaseRunner over SQLToolkit)?
plausible_answers: reuse the shipped infrastructure; only model, grammar, validation and compiler are accounting-specific
standalone as in the original spec
hybrid: reuse audit only, keep SQLToolkit for execution
unknowns.user_answer: Reuse the shipped infrastructure: SemanticAuditLedger (generalising the entry), Executor/ConnectionResolver over DatabaseQueryToolkit and the compile cache; only model, grammar, validation and compiler are accounting-specific.

unknowns.question: Which governance posture do finance metrics get: the shipped fail-closed model (DataPlanePolicyGuard on the journal table + per-role metric grants in a policy side-file) or the original one (DatasetPolicyGuard, per-metric resources, no guard means allow)?
plausible_answers: shipped fail-closed model with a policy side-file
fail-closed guard but per-metric resource names
unknowns.user_answer: The original spec's posture: DatasetPolicyGuard with accounting:<tenant>:<model>:<metric> resources; no guard configured means allow (same as DatasetManager).

unknowns.question: What DuckDB scope does this revision take for FEAT-880: only a DuckDB-over-Arrow runtime fed through a frame_provider (DatasetManager untouched), a reusable in-process DuckDB engine that a later store feature builds on, or the DuckDB-backed dataset store itself?
plausible_answers: reusable engine here, store in its own feature
the dataset store is part of FEAT-713
unknowns.user_answer: Reusable engine here: FEAT-713 delivers an in-process DuckDB-over-Arrow engine (root connection, frame registration, per-thread cursors) designed for reuse; the DuckDB-backed dataset store goes into its own feature that builds on it.

unknowns.question: Where do accounting models live: <models_dir>/<tenant>/<model>.yaml as originally decided, or the shipped flat directory with a policy side-file per model?
plausible_answers: flat directory + policy side-file, tenant from the request context
tenant sub-directories, each with policy side-files
unknowns.user_answer: Tenant sub-directories: <models_dir>/<tenant>/<model>.yaml, as the brainstorm decided.

recommended_next_command.rationale: Localization is high-confidence and the accounting design carries over; the four forks are owner decisions about alignment with the shipped layer, not something more exploration would settle.

meta.notes: Follow-up research for /sdd-spec (answerable by reading): native.py beyond line 140 (windows / CASE handling) to firm up C3; whether DuckDBSource accepts a shared in-memory database; the scheduler bootstrap in ai-parrot-server (old Q11); the FEAT-880 spec being written in the main checkout, to confirm what it expects from this feature.
